eligibility_reason: MemoryManager has exclusive read-write access to a memory bank and executes explicit add/delete/update operations at run time (p. 14, MemoryManager System Prompt: 'add memory | Create new semantic memory entry', 'delete memory | Delete semantic memory entry', Update Operation Workflow); ChatAgent autonomously decides when to query or update this store across conversational turns/sessions via a Query->Generate->Update ReAct loop, and retrieved memory conditions the agent's own future responses (p. 2, p. 4-5). The store is externalised (RawMessageStore + SemanticMemoryStore, p. 4) and agent-written, not a fixed corpus (E3 does not apply) and not parametric-only (E2 does not apply). Published 2026 (post-2023), English, full text present (16 pages, not abstract-only).

facets.justification: Contribution #2 on p. 2 is explicitly the two-tier combination itself: 'Dual-layer hybrid memory with evidence linking. We propose a two-tier memory architecture with progressive narrowing for efficient and precise retrieval.' Section 4.2 (p. 4) defines the two coupled layers -- RawMessageStore (chronological log) and SemanticMemoryStore (embedded semantic entries) -- linked via evidence ids for progressive narrowing between them. The ablation on p. 8 ('Effect of dual-layer memory... degrades performance by 13.31 percentage points') evaluates the coupling itself, confirming the combination, not either store alone, is what the paper argues for.

The MemoryManager system prompt's Update Operation Workflow (p. 14) has the agent 'Decide strategy: CREATE / DELETE / BOTH' after searching for related existing memories, and states 'When updating contradictory info: delete old -> create new -> add update record' -- entries are corrected/replaced as new information arrives, not merely appended. This matches the paper's central framing on p. 1: personalization is repositioned from 'one-shot configuration' to a 'co-evolving memory mechanism' that can 'flexibly update or refine existing concepts,' unlike prior static approaches. (The RawMessageStore layer is separately described as append-only, p. 4, but the Semantic Memory Store -- the layer MemoryManager actively curates -- is the one edited.)

Section 4.2 (p. 4-5) defines three parallel scoring paths -- dense text similarity, BM25 sparse, and cross-modal image similarity (Eqs. 3-5) -- fused by a declared Reciprocal Rank Fusion rule (Eq. 6, k=60) into a single retrieval score. The conclusion (p. 8) names this explicitly: 'Tri-path cross-modal hybrid retrieval combining dense text embeddings, BM25 sparse retrieval, and cross-modal image embeddings provides robust recall.' The ablation 'Effect of tri-path retrieval' (p. 8) evaluates removing individual paths from this fusion, confirming the combination is both declared and measured.

Section 5.3 (p. 8) evaluates on a synthesized benchmark built from LoCoMo plus Yo'LLaVA/MC-LLaVA concept sessions (p. 5, Figure 3), with ablations run on Qwen3VL-8B, GPT-4o-mini, and GLM-4.6V-Flash and results reported as percentage-point deltas (Table 2, Figure 5). No deployment, field use, or real users are reported; the Impact Statement (p. 8) discusses only hypothetical societal consequences, not an actual fielded system. This is a controlled lab investigation, not use in practice.

Evidence comes from a constructed QA benchmark (LoCoMo sessions interpolated with concept-grounded sub-sessions, p. 5, Figure 3) scored via an LLM-as-judge CORRECT/WRONG protocol (p. 15), with the abstract stating 'M2A significantly outperforms baselines' and p. 8 reporting ablation scores across multiple model backbones and conditions (Table 2, Figure 5) -- systems run over a fixed task suite with scores reported, rather than a single manipulated variable against one control.

The paper repeatedly self-describes the contribution as an architecture, not a single technique: p. 1 abstract/intro, 'We propose M2 A, an agentic framework with dual-layer hybrid memory,' and contribution #1 on p. 2, 'We introduce M2 A, an agentic multimodal memory framework that supports incremental concept updates.' The contribution spans multiple organised components -- two collaborating agents (ChatAgent, MemoryManager), a two-tier store with evidence linking, and a tri-path retrieval strategy -- which is the 'architecture or way of organising a system' the framework value covers. Code is released (p. 1) but is presented as an implementation of the architecture, not the argued contribution itself.
